title: Application (25A789) to extend the time to file the reply brief on the merits, submitted to Justice Gorsuch

pages.text:
No. 24-935

IN THE
Supreme Court of the United States

FLOWERS FOODS, INC., ET AL.,
                                                                               Petitioners,
v.
ANGELO BROCK,
                                                                               Respondent.

APPLICATION FOR AN EXTENSION OF TIME
TO FILE PETITIONER’S REPLY BRIEF



To the Honorable Neil M. Gorsuch, Associate Justice of the Supreme Court and
Circuit Justice for the Tenth Circuit:
1. Pursuant to Supreme Court Rule 30.3, Petitioner s Flowers Foods, Inc.,
Flowers Bakeries, LLC, and Flowers Baking Co. of Denver, LLC, respectfully request
an extension of the deadline for Petitioner to file its reply  brief by 10 days  if
Respondent’s pending request for a 10-day extension of time to file his response brief
is granted.  The deadline would extend to and include March 3, 2026.
2. Respondent’s brief is currently due on January 12, 2026, and
Petitioner’s reply brief is currently due on February 11, 2026.
3. Respondent has filed a motion to extend the time to file his response
brief by 10 days, to and including January 22, 2026.
4. Petitioners consented to Respondent’s request for an extension of time
to file his response brief , so long as the Court similarly extend s the reply brief
deadline by ten days, to and including March 3, 2026.

2

5. There is good cause for the extension of the reply brief. Undersigned
counsel has several obligations that would make it difficult to prepare the reply brief
absent an extension.  These include, for example:
a. an oral argument in the Second Circuit in Puris v. TikTok , No. 25 -
322, on January 23, 2026;
b. long-planned client meetings in Brussels, Belgium, the week of
January 26, 2026;
c. a reply brief due on January 29, 2026, in Coleman v. Chevron Corp.,
No. 2:25-cv-10740-MWC-BFM (C.D. Cal.);
d. a petition for certiorari due to this Court on February 19, 2026, in
Aviagames, Inc. v. Pandolfi, see 25A655;
e. and a Second Circuit oral argument noticed for the week of March 16,
2026, in Curtis v. Hilton Worldwide, No. 24-3244.
6. This schedule would permit this case to be heard during the Court’s
March sitting. Petitioners’ reply brief would be due on or before March 3, 2026, and
would therefore be received by the Clerk more than 10 days before the beginning of
the March sitting on March 23, 2026.
WHEREFORE, Petitioners respectfully request that if Respondents pending
motion for an extension is granted, an order be entered extending the time to file the
reply brief by 10 days, up to and including March 3, 2026.

3

January 7, 2026 Respectfully submitted,


/s/ Traci L. Lovitt
TRACI L. LOVITT
Counsel of Record
JONES DAY
250 Vesey Street
New York, New York  10281
(212) 326-3939
tlovitt@jonesday.com

Counsel for Petitioners
